title: Interpret Disabled RMS Charger Button: Charger Assignment Is Controlled by WCS
summary: If an RMS UI charger-related button appears but is disabled/unusable, the expected explanation is that charger assignment and charging management were transferred to WCS. WCS assigns an AGV to a particular charger; RMS does not assign the charger ID, so the RMS charger UI action cannot be used as before.
when_to_use: Use when you see a charger-related button in the RMS UI that is disabled/unusable and you need to interpret what that means for charger assignment responsibility.
not_for: Do not use this procedure as a WCS-side diagnostic guide for why charger assignment fails after WCS control is confirmed.
roles_and_responsibilities: L2_support: Interpret the disabled/unusable RMS charger UI behavior using the WCS responsibility split (WCS assigns the AGV to a charger; RMS does not).
L2_support: If charger assignment still fails after confirming WCS control, escalate for deeper WCS/API investigation (no WCS diagnostic steps are provided in this segment).
access_or_tools_needed: RMS UI access (to observe the charger button state)
WCS knowledge/engagement (responsibility for charger assignment per source)

steps.title: Locate the charger-related button in the RMS UI that may be visible but not usable
steps.purpose: Identify the specific RMS UI control whose disabled/unusable state needs interpretation.
steps.instruction: In the RMS UI, locate the charger-related button that the source indicates may still appear on the UI but is not usable for assigning a charger ID.
steps.expected_result: You can point to the charger-related button in the RMS UI that is present but not usable for charger ID assignment.
steps.healthy_condition: The charger-related button is visible but does not allow the charger ID assignment action (i.e., it is disabled/unusable for that purpose).
steps.failure_condition: You cannot find the charger-related button, or the UI behavior does not match the expected disabled/unusable charger assignment behavior described by the source.

actions.label: Inspect RMS charger button state
actions.exact_action: Locate the charger-related button on the RMS UI that may be visible but not usable.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: “They have transferred the feature over to WCS... it's WCS responsible to assign AGV to a particular charger. The RMS doesn't do it. So even though you see that button on the UI, you can't use it.”

steps.title: Observe whether charger selection/action is disabled (cannot assign charger ID via RMS)
steps.purpose: Confirm the observed RMS UI behavior that indicates charger assignment is not performed by RMS.
steps.instruction: Check whether the charger selection/action is disabled/unusable when you attempt to use the RMS charger-related button to assign a charger ID.
steps.expected_result: The RMS charger-related action is disabled/unusable for assigning a charger ID.
steps.healthy_condition: Attempting to use the RMS charger button does not successfully assign a charger ID (consistent with the WCS control transfer).
steps.failure_condition: The RMS charger button successfully assigns a charger ID (contradicting the WCS responsibility split described by the source), or the UI behavior is inconsistent with the expected disabled/unusable state.

actions.label: Attempt RMS charger assignment action
actions.exact_action: Observe whether the charger selection/action is disabled when attempting to use the RMS charger-related button.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: “...yesterday, like we were trying to send one of the bot to the charger, ... the button ... was starting up with the charger ID cannot. So it's disabled.”

steps.title: Interpret the behavior using the WCS responsibility split (WCS assigns AGV to charger; RMS does not)
steps.purpose: Provide the correct interpretation so the team does not attempt RMS-based charger assignment.
steps.instruction: Use the source explanation to interpret the disabled RMS charger UI behavior: WCS is responsible to assign an AGV to a particular charger; RMS does not assign the charger ID even if a button appears on the UI.
steps.expected_result: You can explain that charger assignment is under WCS control, so RMS charger UI actions may be disabled/unusable even when a button appears.
steps.healthy_condition: Your interpretation matches the source: WCS assigns the AGV to a charger; RMS does not perform charger ID assignment.
steps.failure_condition: You interpret the disabled RMS charger button as an RMS-side malfunction rather than as expected behavior due to WCS control transfer.

actions.label: Apply WCS responsibility interpretation
actions.exact_action: Interpret the disabled/unusable RMS charger button as expected because WCS assigns the AGV to a particular charger and RMS doesn’t.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: “Charger assignment feature transferred to WCS; WCS assigns AGV to a particular charger; RMS doesn’t do it, so even though you see a button on the UI, you can’t use it.”

steps.title: If RMS charger assignment still fails, treat it as expected and escalate for WCS/API investigation
steps.purpose: Handle the case where an operator attempts RMS charger assignment and it fails, without wasting time on RMS-side troubleshooting.
steps.instruction: If attempting to use the RMS charger assignment fails, interpret it as expected given the WCS control transfer described in the segment; then escalate for deeper WCS/API investigation because this segment does not provide WCS-side diagnostic steps.
steps.expected_result: You stop pursuing RMS charger ID assignment and escalate for WCS/API investigation when charger assignment still fails.
steps.healthy_condition: Escalation is initiated for deeper WCS/API investigation rather than continuing RMS UI attempts.
steps.failure_condition: Continuing to troubleshoot RMS charger UI as if RMS should assign the charger ID, despite the WCS responsibility split.

actions.label: Escalate for WCS/API investigation
actions.exact_action: Escalate for deeper WCS/API investigation when charger assignment still fails under WCS control (no WCS diagnostic steps are provided in this segment).

stop_or_escalate_if: Charger assignment still fails after applying the WCS responsibility interpretation (segment provides no WCS-side diagnostic steps).

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: “...it's WCS responsible to assign AGV to a particular charger. The RMS doesn't do it... you can't use it everywhere using the RMS.”

success_criteria: You can correctly explain that charger assignment is controlled by WCS, so RMS charger UI actions may be disabled/unusable even when a button appears.
If charger assignment still fails, you escalate for deeper WCS/API investigation rather than continuing RMS-based charger ID assignment attempts.
healthy_conditions: RMS charger-related button is visible but disabled/unusable for assigning a charger ID.
Interpretation aligns with WCS responsibility: WCS assigns the AGV to a particular charger; RMS does not.
failure_conditions: RMS charger UI appears enabled/usable for charger ID assignment (contradicting the source responsibility split).
Charger assignment still fails and the team does not escalate for WCS/API investigation.
escalation_guidance: If charger assignment still fails after confirming the expected RMS disabled/unusable behavior, escalate for deeper WCS/API investigation. This segment does not include WCS-side diagnostic steps.
